title: The Weekly Marketing Report Your Team Will Actually Read
voiceScript: Most weekly marketing reports are forty charts nobody reads. Someone spends five hours a week building it, about seventy five thousand dollars a year of manager time, and nobody acts on any of it. Here's the test that fixes it. A good report catches things. One team spotted a broken tracking setup in twenty four hours instead of finding it a quarter later. That's the whole job. So cut it to the numbers that change a decision, put the recommendation in the first line, and automate the collecting. ASUS saved ninety hours a week doing exactly that. And the best reports read in under five minutes. Follow for the build.

source: Topic (SM Schedule row 259/267, Jul 30): 'The Weekly Marketing Report Your Team Will Actually Read', reference: Weekly Business Review skill. REGENERATED from the Doc's Source_S tab after v1 was rejected for weak script + visuals. NOTE: v1's headline claim ('about 11 seconds of attention') is NOT supported by the Source tab, which says stakeholders skim reports for ~30 seconds; the 11s figure came from the looser LinkedIn tab and has been dropped rather than repeated. Grounding, all from Source_S: reports with 40+ charts become a 'data graveyard' nobody can find the point in; marketers spend 5+ hours a week copy-pasting numbers, which costs roughly $75,000/year in manager overhead; tracking likes instead of revenue makes executives stop trusting the data. What GOOD reports do: one team caught a technical tracking break in 24 HOURS rather than weeks/a quarter; ASUS saved 90 HOURS PER WEEK by automating their data pulls; high-performing reports read in UNDER 5 MINUTES and lead with 'what do we do next?'. Benchmarks available if needed: CTR 2-5% search / 0.5-1.5% social, ROAS 3-5x ecom / 2x+ B2B, conversion 1-3% B2B / 0.5-2% ecom. POV SHIFT vs v1: v1 argued 'cut to six numbers and lead with the answer' (generic); v2 argues a report's real job is to CATCH things, and time-to-catch is the test that separates a live instrument from a document. SIGNATURE = a TRIPWIRE ON A METRIC LINE: a tangle of ~14 faint chart lines (the 40-chart graveyard) strips down to ONE clean line with a dashed threshold tripwire beneath it; the line dips, CROSSES the wire, and an alert fires instantly stamped '24 HRS' - contrasted against a ghosted version where the same dip passes unnoticed inside the tangle while a month strip runs a full quarter before a late flag appears. Recurring texture = the line crossing the wire and how long until anyone notices. NO agency name / no university (personal-brand content); first person. Voice generated at --speed 0.76 (slower corrected pace).
